visualization.scatter plot: Use when exploring relationships or trends between two continuous variables.
visualization.heatmap: Use to visualize correlation matrix for multiple numerical variables.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Use Pearson correlation when both variables are normally distributed.
Step 2: Use Spearman correlation if data is ordinal or non-parametric assumptions hold.
Step 3: Use linear regression when modeling the relationship or prediction between two numerical variables.

visualization.grouped boxplot: Use to compare the distribution of numerical values across categories.
visualization.violin plot: Use when visualizing both distribution shape and spread across groups.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Use t-test for comparing two group means (binary categorical variable) with normal numerical data.
Step 2: Use ANOVA for comparing means across 3+ groups with normal numerical data.
Step 3: Use Mann-Whitney U test when normality assumption is violated or data is ordinal.

visualization.mosaic plot: Use to display proportions and interactions in contingency tables.
visualization.stacked bar chart: Use to visually compare the distribution of one categorical variable across another.

selection_criteria: Step 1: Use chi-square test for large sample sizes to test independence between two categorical variables.
Step 2: Use Fisher's exact test when sample size is small or expected cell frequencies < 5.
Step 3: Use Cramér's V to measure the strength of association between two categorical variables.
